IRB Barcelona is seeking a highly motivated and talented Postdoctoral Fellow to participate in cutting edge research line of the Quantitative Stem Cell Dynamics lab led by Alejo Rodriguez-Fraticelli.

The lab focuses on developing cutting-edge single-cell tracing technologies to cellular memory in normal and premalignant hematopoietic stem cells. The goal of this project is to identify the mechanisms that generate stem cell memories across a wide range of perturbations.

We are looking for a wet lab candidate with a strong background in hematology, with a proven evidence in the field of epigenetic analysis and/or stem cell research. Knowledge of single-cell techniques, clonal barcoding, fluorescence activated cell sorting, biostatistics, and/or genomics will be appreciated but is not required for this position and the candidates will be trained in all appropriate skills for this project.

This position is funded by the project “Cartograms of hematopoietic responses to extrinsic perturbations” financed by La Caixa (LCF/PR/HR26- 00990). The position is for 2 years, with the potential to extend this contract up to 1 additional year. This level of support makes this an excellent opportunity for candidates looking to transition to an independent research-focused position.

KEY RESPONSABILITIES

  • Independently design and test biological hypotheses.

  • Plan, perform and interpret experiments.

  • Collaborate with a multidisciplinary research team, tapping into the expertise of fellow researchers and external collaborators.

  • Contribute to a culture of scientific excellence, efficiency, and teamwork.

  • Contribute to other lab projects and to the maintenance of protocols and laboratory resources in the group.

  • Critically analyze analytical results, participate in scientific discussions and in preparation of diverse forms of scientific communication (seminars and conferences).

  • Participate in the project activities: meetings, presentations, visits to other labs, collaboration, exchange of data sets, preparing project reports/deliverables.

  • Perform excellent research according to the high standards of the lab and the IRB Barcelona.

YOU HAVE

  • PhD in a relevant Life Sciences field.

  • At least one publication as first-author in a top-ranked journal (ranked Q1 in a life sciences field)

  • Experience in hematological malignancies, including ex vivo and in vivo experiments.

  • Demonstrated ability to design and conduct experiments independently, particularly in mouse models of HSC biology or immunology.

  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively.

  • Strong organizational and multitasking skills.

  • Attention to detail and accuracy.

  • Proficiency in English (both written and spoken).

  • Highly motivated, enthusiastic and collaborative person.

  • Willing to keep on learning.

  • Ability to work independently in a demanding research environment.

YOU MIGHT ALSO HAVE

  • Familiarity with stem cell memory experiments and bone marrow transplantation.

  • Experience with cellular barcoding techniques.

  • Independent capacity to operate a fluorescence-activated cell sorter.

  • Ability to secure additional funding, such as grant-writing or fellowship-writing skills.

WHAT WE OFFER:

To be a part a part of something meaningful: We are a biomedical research centre that tirelessly works to achieve a society free of diseases. Our mission is to carry out research of excellence to cure cancer and other diseases linked to ageing.

IRB Barcelona is seeking a talented and highly motivated Postdoctoral Researcher to join the Structural Bioinformatics and Network Biology group (https://sbnb.irbbarcelona.org), led by Dr. Patrick Aloy, to work on Systems Medicine approaches in the context of the CLARITY European collaborative project.

Viral infections, together with human genetics, constitute major risk factors for developing complex diseases. However, the molecular and physiological mechanisms of how these viral infections cause and contribute to non-communicable disease development are unknown thus hampering prevention and therapeutic approaches. CLARITY will take advantage of cutting-edge experimental technologies and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven analytics to elucidate the molecular and physiological mechanisms of how RSV infection (infectious disease) contributes to asthma (non-communicable disease) development.

In particular, we will use modern AI techniques to integrate the generated RSV data with the bulk of current biomedical knowledge and derive RSV perturbation signatures. We will then compare these signatures to those of non-communicable human diseases, and implement a strategy to discover causal relationships between them. Finally, we will identify and validate drug-like molecules with the potential to revert the RSV perturbation induced changes in vitro, and provide initial lead compounds for further development.

This position is co-financed by the project Causative Link between respiratory syncytial virus and chronic lung diseases: Identifying Targets for Teraphy de la Comisión Europea. Acrónimo: CLARITY. Grant Agreement: 101137201.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

The successful candidate will work in a very collaborative environment, where he/she will be responsible for the integration of all the data generated within the consortium into the embeddings space of the Chemical Checker (Duran-Frigola et al. Nat Biotechnol 2020; Bertoni et al. Nat Commun 2021; Comajuncosa-Creus et al. Nat Protocols 2025) and the Bioteque (Fernández-Torras et al. Nat Commun 2022) as well as the development of the new signatures to define the perturbed modules. Additionally, he/she will also be responsible for developing the comparative methods to link the effects of viral-perturbations to the signatures of non-communicable common diseases.

Finally, he/she will adapt the generative-AI models available in the group to identify or design new chemical compounds with the capacity to stop the progression from RSV-induced cellular perturbations to the onset of related non-communicable diseases.

YOU HAVE:

  • Education: Bachelor in Biosciences, or Engineering degree in Computer or Data Sciences. PhD in bioinformatics, data sciences, machine learning or related areas.

  • Experience: previous experience working with multi-omics data and the use of machine learning and data science techniques. Strong publications record according to his/her career stage.

  • Skills:

    • Excellent programming and scripting skills, with deep knowledge of Python.

    • Excellent knowledge of machine learning packages (Scikit, Keras, Pytorch, etc).

    • Competent in the use of HPC systems, virtual machines (OpenNebula) and Grid Containers (Docker, Singularity).

    • Highly motivated. Excellent interpersonal and communication skills. Fluency in English.

A plus for the candidate would be to have previous experience in using LLMs programmatically, for example, as part of RAG or agentic systems.

The candidate will participate and perform the activities, tasks, and reports within the framework of the project AURORA.

sections.html:
IRB Barcelona is seeking a proactive and motivated AI Software Engineer to join the Biomedical Genomics Lab (BBGLab) led by Dr. Núria López-Bigas at IRB Barcelona (bbglab.irbbarcelona.org).

The lab studies the mutations and mechanisms that drive cancer development, and translates this knowledge into computational tools for research and precision cancer medicine. AI is becoming a central part of this work, both to accelerate scientific discovery and to make the lab's tools more useful to researchers and clinicians.

The successful candidate will join a team of bioinformaticians and software engineers to build AI-powered systems, with a strong focus on LLMs and agentic systems. Current projects include an agentic AI system for human-AI scientific collaboration, co-developed with the lab's researchers to uncover the molecular mechanisms of tumorigenesis across genes and tissues, and a chatbot embedded in the Cancer Genome Interpreter to support the interpretation of mutations.

The role is mainly focused on engineering, with some support to research projects. Prior experience in cancer genomics or bioinformatics is not essential, but it is considered an asset; we are looking for someone curious about the biology behind our work and willing to learn it.

This position is financed by the project “Data-driven cancer genome interpretation for personalised cancer treatment” from the European Union (Acronim: CGI-Clinics. Grant Agreement: 101057509).

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Design, develop, deploy and maintain LLM-based and agentic applications for the lab's projects, such as the agentic system for scientific collaboration and the Cancer Genome Interpreter chatbot.

  • Integrate AI components with the lab's tools, databases and knowledge sources.

  • Evaluate and improve the quality and reliability of LLM-based systems (prompting, context management, tool use, evaluation).

  • Apply software engineering best practices: version control, testing, code review and documentation.

  • Keep up to date with advances in AI and propose how to apply them to the lab's projects.

  • Provide technical support to research projects, participate in project meetings, and contribute to technical reports.

YOU HAVE

  • Highly proactive profile, with a strong willingness to learn and to stay constantly up to date with a rapidly changing AI landscape (models, frameworks, tools and AI coding assistants).

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Bioinformatics, Computational Sciences, Physics, Mathematics or similar.

  • At least 1 year of experience in software development.

  • Hands-on experience with LLMs and agentic systems (e.g. LLM APIs, prompt and context engineering, RAG, tool use, agents).

  • Strong Python programming skills and familiarity with software development best practices.

  • Experience with collaborative software development using Git and platforms such as GitHub.

  • Excellent English (written and spoken).

  • Excellent communication skills and ability to work within a collaborative team.

  • Strong analytical skills, ability to work independently, and adaptability to new challenges.

YOU MIGHT ALSO HAVE

  • Extensive, proven experience building LLM-based applications and agentic systems (RAG, MCP, multi-agent frameworks, evaluation).

  • Experience with AI coding assistants and modern AI development workflows.

  • Experience with machine learning or deep learning.

  • Experience in bioinformatics or cancer genomics, particularly in NGS data analysis.

  • Experience with pipelines (Nextflow), high-performance computing, containers (Docker, Singularity), cloud environments (e.g. AWS), and databases.

  • Experience with full-stack development.

  • A Master’s degree or a PhD in a related field.

  • Experience working in international teams.

IRB Barcelona is seeking a highly motivated and talented Postdoctoral Fellow to participate in cutting edge research line of the Molecular Biophysics Research Group led by Dr. Xavier Salvatella.

This position is co-funded by project AY2AX000267, under the Biogami 2026 Call, funded by the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Independently design and test hypotheses regarding the conformational and oligomerization properties of intrinsically disordered proteins or regions of proteins.

  • Plan, perform and interpret using solution nuclear magnetic resonance experiments.

  • Collaborate with a multidisciplinary research team, tapping into the expertise of fellow researchers and external collaborators.

  • Contribute to a culture of scientific excellence, efficiency, and teamwork.

  • Contribute to other lab projects and to the maintenance of protocols and laboratory resources in the group.

  • Critically analyze analytical results, participate in scientific discussions and in preparation of diverse forms of scientific communication (seminars and conferences).

  • Participate in the project activities: meetings, presentations, visits to other labs, collaboration, exchange of data sets, preparing project reports/deliverables.

  • Perform excellent research according to the high standards of the lab and the IRB Barcelona.

YOU HAVE

  • PhD in chemistry/physics/biochemistry/biotechnology or a related field.

  • Demonstrated ability to design and conduct solution nuclear magnetic resonance experiments independently.

  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively.

  • Strong organizational and multitasking skills.

  • Attention to detail and accuracy.
